reason: (1) Stationary measure of an r-adding walk on a cyclic group is uniform on the group (doubly-stochastic translation operator); the induced law of x(P) is the uniform-on-E pushforward, and #{P in E: x(P) in V} = 2|V|(1+O(2^{-n/2}poly)) by Weil/Kohel-Shparlinski additive-character sums (the indicator of V is a sum of 2^{n-l} additive characters, each giving O(sqrt q) error). So any stationary hitting bias is beta=1+O(2^{-n/2}). (2) Transient correlation: the walk partition uses x mod r (representation-dependent), but its spectral gap is a property of the Cayley-type graph on the group (Teske/Hildebrand-Hildebrand mixing ~ poly(log) steps); an x-mod-V observable is just a test function, and its autocorrelation decays at that same rate; no observable can create mass not in the stationary law beyond O(mixing-time) steps. (3) Even with beta>1, V-membership is a membership test on a walk built from group operations + x-partition, i.e. a generic oracle with a representation-dependent hash; yield per target improves by at most beta, so B*D^2 vs N unchanged (CGK line not crossed). Class: engineering at best, measured null.

computed.setup: binary curves y^2+xy=x^3+x^2+a6, r=20 adding walk keyed by x mod 20, 1e5 steps, 8 random V with l=floor(n/2)
computed.summary: all 32 ratios within ~2.4 sigma of 1; pooled mean ratio ~1.00; no growth with n

obstruction: Weil bound (Kohel-Shparlinski) on stationary law + group-determined mixing + CGK generic oracle bound
scope: Does not cover walks whose step choice depends on non-linear field structure designed to steer (not a translation walk), nor non-stationary short-walk tails shorter than mixing time; spectral-gap-on-2^8-classes check not run (mean-frequency test suffices since stationary law is fixed).
